scenes.title: Flink Table API
scenes.subtitle: build, run, and debug, in compose or kubernetes
scenes.narration: Welcome. [[slnc 400]] In the next few minutes, you will see how to build, [[slnc 200]] run, [[slnc 200]] and [[emph +]]debug an Apache Flink job using the Table A P I. [[slnc 600]] We will cover both docker compose, [[slnc 200]] and kubernetes, [[slnc 200]] and we will attach a debugger to the running cluster from your I D E.

scenes.title: What you will learn
scenes.body:
1. Bring up a Flink session cluster in two ways
2. Build an uber-jar with a Table API job
3. Submit it from the command line and the Web UI
4. Watch records flow through the operators
5. Attach IntelliJ or VSCode to the live JVM
6. Use suspend equals y to pause at startup
scenes.narration: Here is the plan. [[slnc 400]] First, we bring up a small Flink session cluster, [[slnc 200]] either with docker compose, or with kubernetes. [[slnc 500]] Then we build an uber jar containing a Table A P I example. [[slnc 400]] We submit it, watch the records flow, [[slnc 300]] and finally we attach a remote debugger from our I D E, [[slnc 200]] and step through real operator code.

scenes.title: Prerequisites
scenes.body:
• Docker, or Rancher Desktop with kubernetes enabled
• Java 11 and Maven, for building the example
• An IDE that speaks JDWP
   IntelliJ IDEA, or VSCode with the Java extension pack
• Optional: the lakehouse stack from spark_minio_trino,
   if you want to run the Kafka example
scenes.narration: You will need docker, [[slnc 200]] or rancher desktop with kubernetes turned on. [[slnc 400]] Java eleven and maven, [[slnc 200]] to build the examples. [[slnc 400]] And an I D E that supports remote J V M debug. [[slnc 300]] If you want to try the kafka example, you will also need the lakehouse stack from the spark minio trino project.

scenes.title: Path 1 — docker compose, the fast path
scenes.code:
cd flink-tutorial
./scripts/build.sh        # mvn package, builds the uber-jar
./scripts/up.sh           # JM + TM + JDWP + Web UI
./scripts/submit.sh com.example.flink.HelloTableApi
scenes.narration: Let us start with docker compose, [[slnc 200]] the fastest path. [[slnc 400]] You change into the flink tutorial directory, [[slnc 300]] run build dot s h, [[slnc 200]] which packages an uber jar with maven, [[slnc 400]] then up dot s h, [[slnc 200]] which brings up a job manager, [[slnc 200]] a task manager, [[slnc 200]] and exposes the web U I. [[slnc 500]] Finally, submit dot s h sends a hello world Table A P I job to the cluster.

scenes.title: Cluster topology
scenes.caption: JM coordinates, TM runs the operators, your IDE attaches over JDWP
scenes.narration: Here is the topology. [[slnc 400]] Your I D E builds an uber jar, [[slnc 300]] which gets submitted to the job manager. [[slnc 400]] The job manager plans the query, [[slnc 200]] then schedules operators onto one or more task managers. [[slnc 500]] The web U I lives on port one eight zero three zero, [[slnc 200]] and the J D W P debugger ports are open on both J V Ms.

scenes.title: Open the Web UI
scenes.body:
Browse to http://127.0.0.1:18030

• Running Jobs shows the hello-world job
• Click into it → Task Managers tab → Stdout
• You will see the print connector dump windowed results

The UI also lets you submit jars by drag-and-drop
(web.submit.enable is on by default for this tutorial)
scenes.narration: Open your browser to one twenty seven dot zero dot zero dot one, port one eight zero three zero. [[slnc 500]] You will see the running jobs panel. [[slnc 400]] Click into the hello world job, [[slnc 200]] go to the task managers tab, [[slnc 200]] and click into the running task manager. [[slnc 400]] The standard out tab shows the print connector dumping each window's results, [[slnc 200]] one row every thirty seconds.

scenes.title: Path 2 — kubernetes
scenes.code:
./scripts/build.sh         # same jar, k8s consumes it
./scripts/k8s-up.sh        # apply manifests, wait for ready
./scripts/k8s-submit.sh com.example.flink.HelloTableApi

# Web UI:
#   NodePort:  http://localhost:30030
#   forward:   kubectl -n flink-tutorial port-forward svc/flink-jobmanager 18030:8081
scenes.narration: Path two, [[slnc 200]] kubernetes. [[slnc 400]] The exact same uber jar works here, [[slnc 200]] you do not have to rebuild. [[slnc 500]] Run k eight s up dot s h to apply the manifests, [[slnc 200]] then k eight s submit dot s h to send the job. [[slnc 500]] The web U I is reachable two ways. [[slnc 300]] As a node port, on localhost three zero zero three zero, [[slnc 300]] or via kubectl port forward, [[slnc 200]] which is what I usually do for ephemeral access.

scenes.title: JobManager versus TaskManager
scenes.left_body:
• Runs main() of your job
• Plans the query
• Builds the JobGraph
• Coordinates checkpoints

For Table API:
SQL planning + optimization
lives here.
scenes.right_body:
• Runs the operators
• Per-record logic
• Joins, windows, aggregations
• Most state lives here

For Table API:
Generated runtime code
runs here. ← debug here.
scenes.narration: Before we attach the debugger, [[slnc 200]] one important distinction. [[slnc 500]] The job manager runs your job's main method only at submit time. [[slnc 400]] It plans the query, [[slnc 200]] builds the job graph, [[slnc 200]] then hands work to the task managers. [[slnc 500]] The task manager is where the [[emph +]]operators run. [[slnc 200]] Per record logic, [[slnc 200]] joins, [[slnc 200]] windows, [[slnc 200]] aggregations. [[slnc 400]] So when you want to know what your data is actually doing, [[slnc 300]] you attach to the [[emph +]]task manager.

scenes.title: JDWP — already on, ready to attach
scenes.body:
Both JVMs boot with:

  -agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=n,address=*:5005

Compose maps the host ports for you:
scenes.code:
| JVM         | Host port      |
|-------------|----------------|
| JobManager  | localhost:18040 |
| TaskManager | localhost:18041 |
scenes.narration: Both J V Ms boot with the J D W P agent enabled. [[slnc 400]] Server equals yes, [[slnc 200]] suspend equals no, [[slnc 200]] which means the J V M starts normally and accepts a debugger whenever you connect. [[slnc 500]] In compose, [[slnc 200]] the host ports are already mapped for you. [[slnc 300]] One eight zero four zero for the job manager, [[slnc 300]] one eight zero four one for the task manager.

scenes.title: Attach via kubernetes — port-forward
scenes.code:
# JobManager
kubectl -n flink-tutorial port-forward \
  svc/flink-jobmanager 18040:5005 &

# TaskManager
kubectl -n flink-tutorial port-forward \
  svc/flink-taskmanager 18041:5005 &

annotations.text: if the TM pod restarts, restart the port-forward

scenes.narration: On kubernetes, [[slnc 200]] J D W P is on container port five thousand and five inside each pod. [[slnc 400]] You open a kubectl port forward in a terminal and leave it running. [[slnc 400]] One for the job manager, [[slnc 200]] one for the task manager. [[slnc 500]] Note, [[slnc 200]] if the task manager pod restarts, [[slnc 200]] you need to restart the port forward as well.

scenes.title: IntelliJ IDEA — Remote JVM Debug
scenes.body:
1. Run → Edit Configurations → + → Remote JVM Debug
2. Debugger mode: Attach to remote JVM
3. Host: localhost
4. Port: 18041 (TaskManager) or 18040 (JobManager)
5. Module classpath: flink-table-tutorial
6. Save → Run → connects within a second

Set a breakpoint in your Table API code,
submit the job, watch records hit the breakpoint.
scenes.narration: In IntelliJ, [[slnc 200]] go to run, [[slnc 200]] edit configurations, [[slnc 200]] add a remote J V M debug configuration. [[slnc 500]] Debugger mode is attach to remote J V M. [[slnc 300]] Host is localhost. [[slnc 300]] Port one eight zero four one for the task manager, [[slnc 200]] or one eight zero four zero for the job manager. [[slnc 400]] Pick the flink table tutorial module on the classpath. [[slnc 400]] Save, [[slnc 200]] run the configuration, [[slnc 200]] and IntelliJ connects in under a second. [[slnc 400]] Set a breakpoint in your Table A P I code, [[slnc 200]] submit the job, [[slnc 200]] and watch records hit your breakpoint as they flow through.

scenes.title: VSCode — launch.json
scenes.narration: VS code is just as simple. [[slnc 300]] Add a configuration to dot vs code slash launch dot json. [[slnc 400]] Type java, [[slnc 200]] request attach, [[slnc 200]] hostname localhost, [[slnc 200]] port one eight zero four one. [[slnc 500]] Then run and debug, [[slnc 200]] attach to flink task manager.

scenes.title: Pause until the debugger attaches
scenes.body:
Need to step through main() or query plan generation?
Flip suspend on, and the JVM blocks until you connect.
scenes.code:
# Compose: just set the env var
FLINK_DEBUG_SUSPEND=y ./scripts/up.sh

# Kubernetes: edit suspend=n → suspend=y in
#   k8s/20-jobmanager.yaml or k8s/30-taskmanager.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/

annotations.text: do NOT use suspend=y on the TaskManager — it hangs job submission

scenes.narration: Sometimes you want to step through main, [[slnc 200]] or watch the Table A P I plan being generated. [[slnc 400]] For that, you need the J V M to pause at startup, [[slnc 200]] until your debugger attaches. [[slnc 500]] In compose, [[slnc 200]] set flink debug suspend to y, [[slnc 200]] and run up dot s h. [[slnc 400]] In kubernetes, [[slnc 200]] edit the manifest, [[slnc 200]] flip suspend equals n to y, [[slnc 200]] and reapply. [[slnc 500]] One warning. [[slnc 300]] [[emph +]]Never set suspend equals y on the task manager, [[slnc 200]] or job submission will hang forever.

scenes.title: Port map — what is reachable where
scenes.narration: Here is the full port map. [[slnc 400]] All host ports live in the eighteen thousand range, [[slnc 200]] coordinated through devportal, [[slnc 200]] so nothing collides with the lakehouse stack on the same machine. [[slnc 500]] Web U I on one eight zero three zero. [[slnc 300]] J D W P on one eight zero four zero, [[slnc 200]] and one eight zero four one.

scenes.title: Common gotchas
scenes.body:
• Connectors are NOT on the cluster classpath
   bundle flink-connector-kafka, flink-json, etc into your uber-jar
   (the example pom does this with the shade plugin)

• TaskManager only sees jars submitted with the job
   dropping jars into JM /opt/flink/lib without TM = ClassNotFoundException

• JDWP does not authenticate
   fine on a dev laptop, never expose port 5005 elsewhere

• web.submit.enable is on by default
   anyone reachable can submit jars — keep this off the open internet
scenes.narration: A few gotchas to watch for. [[slnc 500]] Flink's connectors are [[emph +]]not on the cluster classpath by default. [[slnc 300]] You need to bundle them into your uber jar, [[slnc 200]] which the example pom does for you with the shade plugin. [[slnc 500]] The task manager only sees jars submitted with the job. [[slnc 200]] Dropping a jar into the job manager's lib directory will give you class not found errors at run time. [[slnc 500]] J D W P does not authenticate, [[slnc 200]] so do not expose port five thousand and five outside your laptop. [[slnc 500]] And the web U I has submission enabled, [[slnc 200]] so do not put it on the open internet.

scenes.title: Tear down and you are done
scenes.code:
# Compose
./scripts/down.sh

# Kubernetes
./scripts/k8s-down.sh

# Both are idempotent — safe to run twice.
scenes.narration: When you are finished, [[slnc 200]] tear the cluster down with down dot s h, [[slnc 200]] or k eight s down dot s h. [[slnc 400]] Both are safe to run twice.
